text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The tracks of the bankruptcy case of Kredito Bankas lead to Russia. The owner, Vladislav Kliukovski, and the head of the board, Sigitas Gecys, have been indicted on charges of swindling and falsifying official documents.
- The Economy ministry drew up a draft project to decentralise Lietuvos Energija heating sector and to pass its functions to municipalities by July 1, 1997 at the latest.

- The heads of companies, their deputies and members of boards will have to declare their property and income acquired in 1996 before March 1, 1997. The declaration of property and income for all people will become obligatory in two years.
- Foreign investors have grown interested in the privatisation of big companies in Lithuania, Nomura International said during a meeting with Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius on Friday.
- Well-known envioronment expert Valdas Adamkus confirmed that he will continue to participate in the country's political life and be a candidate in forthcoming presidential elections.

- Polish President Alexander Kwasniewski and the chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbergis said during a meeting on Saturday in Warsaw that Russia's diplomats will not succeed in postponing the adoption of new members to NATO.
